result.rationale: The diff shows `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent. When externalCalendarId is falsy, the find predicate compares against the same falsy value and can never match, so calendarId is undefined; the prior code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same dead-fallback pattern appears in updateEvent. Behavior regression when references lack externalCalendarId.

judged_text: In deleteEvent the same pattern `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match and yields undefined Cancelling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId now calls `calendar.events.delete` with `calendarId: undefined` (previously fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`); the delete fails and the orphaned event stays on the attendee's Google calendar while the cancellation flow completes

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` change the fallback calendar selection to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Since that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null/""`, the `.find(...)` condition can never match a real destination calendar externalId, so the result is effectively always `undefined` (unless a calendar has an undefined externalId). This is a real logic defect introduced by the diff: it no longer reliably falls back to the event’s destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing, which can cause deletes/updates to target the wrong calendar (or potentially an undefined calendarId depending on downstream usage).
